name: Serbian nationalism
summary: Serbian nationalism is an ethnic nationalism holding that Serbs form one nation whose cultural and political unity should be secured, ideally in a single state. It centres on the Kosovo myth, the Serbian Orthodox Church as the core of national identity, opposition to the secession of territories claimed as Serbian, and a Greater Serbia tradition running from Garasanin's 1844 programme through the 1986 Memorandum to the Radical Party and Dveri. Today's parties are Eurosceptic, anti-NATO, Russia-leaning and socially conservative.
scope: The mainstream contemporary and late-Yugoslav strand: the Karadzic language-based definition of Serbs, Garasanin's Nacertanije (1844), the 1986 SANU Memorandum, the Milosevic-era mobilisation, and present-day parties such as the Serbian Radical Party and Dveri. Economic and many social answers are low-confidence inferences because the sources document national, religious and foreign-policy positions far better. It excludes the Yugoslavist-liberal reading of Garasanin and Karadzic, and treats the Chetnik and Seselj expulsion programmes as a militant strand.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The sources say little on health policy; the Serbian right's pronatalist family agenda and statist habits suggest support for state-provided care, inferred rather than stated.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Nationalist sources give no wage programme and economic views inside the movement range from populist to liberal, so no clear side.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Economic nationalism and protectionism are listed SRS principles, which implies distrust of unfettered markets, though no market-versus-state doctrine is documented.

public-ownership.rationale: Economic nationalism and a long Serbian tradition of state-owned utilities and infrastructure point toward public ownership of strategic industry; inferred.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The sources record no tax doctrine; populist parties of this strand attack elites but nationalism does not dictate a tax position.

unions-good.rationale: Labour organisation is not a nationalist theme in these sources; adherents can cite class cooperation or hostility to unions equally.

property-fundamental.rationale: No documented position; protection of property is secondary to national questions and the strand includes both statist and propertarian voices.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Anti-globalisation and economic nationalism imply hostility to foreign corporate power, inferred from SRS principles.

cut-welfare.rationale: Populist and family-oriented nationalists generally avoid welfare retrenchment; inferred from the pronatalist family agenda in Dveri's platform.

worker-ownership.rationale: Not a nationalist theme; the strand's property outlook is closer to private and state ownership than to cooperatives, inferred.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Counter-terrorism surveillance is not addressed; security-minded instincts pull one way and anti-state suspicion of governments pulls the other.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Described as traditionalist and socially conservative, so recreational drug legalisation would be opposed; inferred.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Nationalist parties have themselves been accused of hate speech and the strand resists such limits; inferred from SRS record.

strong-leader.rationale: Milosevic-era mobilisation centred on a single national leader and the strand favours decisive executive power, though democratic parties of the strand also compete in elections.

state-harmful.rationale: Serbian nationalism is a state-building project aimed at a unified Serbian state, so denying the need for a state contradicts its core.

limit-guns.rationale: No documented position; Balkan gun culture and conservatism lean permissive while security politics lean restrictive.

empower-police-military.rationale: The SRS advocated force over Kosovo and the strand glorifies military heroism, so more resources for security forces is the typical position.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Socially conservative and Church-aligned parties of the strand oppose legalisation; inferred.

decide-locally.rationale: The nationalist programme sought to end the autonomy of Kosovo and Vojvodina and favoured a centralised Serbian and Yugoslav state ('Strong Serbia, Strong Yugoslavia').

rehabilitation.rationale: Conservative law-and-order outlook favours punishment over rehabilitation; inferred, not stated in sources.

traditional-family.rationale: Dveri proposes a Ministry for the Family and describes itself as family oriented, and the SRS is documented as traditionalist and socially conservative.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Dveri openly opposes gay pride marches and the SRS is socially conservative; Church-aligned nationalism strongly rejects same-sex marriage.

abortion-legal.rationale: Dveri openly opposes abortion as part of its population-rebuilding agenda, though not every nationalist party shares this.

more-religion-public.rationale: From the late 1980s Orthodoxy was promoted as the spiritual basis and most essential component of Serbian national identity.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not a Serbian nationalist theme; the strand's conservatism and ethnic-nation outlook make active racial redress unlikely, inferred.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Family-centred, Church-aligned traditionalism implies belief in natural gender roles; inferred from Dveri positions.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Defending Serbian cultural and spiritual identity, from Karadzic's language work to the Church-backed national revival, is the heart of the ideology.

gradual-change.rationale: Adherents have both called for radical national mobilisation and defended continuity of tradition, so no consistent stance.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Anti-immigration is among the SRS's listed principles.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The strand opposes EU and NATO and sees Western-led institutions as hostile over Kosovo, though Dveri wants Kosovo talks returned to the UN.

free-trade.rationale: Protectionism and opposition to globalisation are listed SRS principles.

nation-first.rationale: Placing the interests of the Serbian nation above outside commitments runs through Garasanin's programme and the 1986 Memorandum's call for Serbia to follow its own national interest.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The 1999 NATO intervention over Kosovo is the central grievance, and Dveri calls NATO a criminal organisation, so humanitarian war is rejected; inferred from the NATO stance.

open-borders.rationale: With anti-immigration politics and an ethnic definition of the nation, open borders is directly opposed.

limit-growth.rationale: Environmental limits to growth are not addressed in nationalist sources and the strand has no consistent view.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: No documented position; nationalists neither centre nor reject climate policy.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: No documented position and the traditionalist outlook cuts against technological optimism while modernising nationalists favour it.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Nuclear power is not addressed in the sources and adherents have no shared view.

revolution-justified.rationale: Serbian nationalism celebrates national uprisings against Ottoman rule but nationalist parties today work through elections, so adherents are split.

experts-over-public.rationale: Populist anti-elite rhetoric favours the people over technocrats; inferred.

central-planning.rationale: Hostile to Titoist economics, which the Memorandum blamed for subordinating Serbia; no explicit stance on planning itself.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not a nationalist theme; no stated position.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; adherents have no shared view.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Family-oriented conservatism tends to defend inheritance; inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Protectionism is a listed principle of the SRS.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Economic nationalism suggests state guidance of strategic sectors; inferred.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Serbia's peasant-smallholder tradition and family emphasis imply support for broadly spread property; inferred.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Anachronistic for the ideology; rejected by inference from its nation-first, property-respecting outlook.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed; the strand does not campaign against central banks.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; no consistent adherent position.

one-party-rule.rationale: Nationalist parties compete in multiparty elections; Milosevic's party dominated but did not claim an ideological single-party right.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The strand includes both royalists linked to the Karadjordjevic dynasty and republicans, so adherents are split.

democracy-best.rationale: Nationalists accept electoral democracy but the Memorandum-era movement subordinated it to national aims; split.

workers-councils.rationale: Class-based councils run against a nation-centred politics; inferred.

right-to-secede.rationale: Serbian nationalists opposed the secession of Croatia, Bosnia and Kosovo and demanded all Serbs be kept in a common state.

natural-rulers.rationale: Not documented; populist anti-elite stance leans against it.

political-violence-never.rationale: The Chetnik tradition and Seselj's advocacy of force show violence is not ruled out by the strand, though many adherents reject it.

war-builds-character.rationale: The Kosovo cult of heroism and sacrifice, as in Milosevic's Gazimestan speech, glorifies armed struggle; inferred.

separate-church-state.rationale: The late-1980s Serbian state embraced the Orthodox Church as central to national identity, so strict separation is disfavoured.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The Church is revered as a national institution but there is no demand for law derived from scripture; inferred.

private-courts-defense.rationale: A strongly state-centred nationalism cannot accept privatised defence; inferred.

military-superiority.rationale: Pro-military, but Serbia's size makes supremacy an unlikely stated aim; inferred.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The movement is described as an ethnic nationalism that defines Serbs as a nation and seeks their unity.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Nationalism treats the nation as the driving historical actor, and the movement rejected communist historiography.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Not an emphasis; inferred from conservative orientation.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed; claims of Serbian historical roots in Kosovo cut one way while the wording points to colonial-era indigenous peoples.

civilizational-union.rationale: Russophilia and Orthodox solidarity are documented, suggesting favour for Orthodox or Slavic political alignment; inferred.

self-interest-moral.rationale: A nationalism of duty and sacrifice sits poorly with an ethic of individual self-interest; inferred.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The nation and community are placed above the individual in the strand's collectivist framing; inferred.

limit-population.rationale: Dveri's Ministry for the Family aims to rebuild Serbia's population, the opposite of limiting growth.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Not a theme; the strand is pro-development, inferred.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Traditionalist, continuity-minded nationalism disfavours disruptive change; inferred.

human-enhancement.rationale: Church-aligned conservatives are wary of bodily enhancement; inferred.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Populist politics resist technocratic delegation; inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: The movement draws legitimacy from medieval Kosovo and a restored national state, though it also pursues new state projects.

results-over-ideology.rationale: No documented position; adherents are ideologically committed but pragmatic in office.

direct-action.rationale: Nationalist parties contest elections, though militant strands exist; inferred.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Wholly outside the ideology's concerns; rejected by inference.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Wholly outside the ideology; rejected by inference.

distribute-by-need.rationale: A communist formula opposed by anti-communist and nation-first nationalists; inferred.

production-for-use.rationale: A socialist principle not adopted by the strand; inferred.

profit-exploitation.rationale: A Marxist claim; nationalism frames exploitation as national rather than class-based, as in the Memorandum's complaint about Serbia's economic subordination.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Nationalism puts the nation above class, and the movement attacked the Titoist communist legacy.

collective-farming.rationale: Serbia's smallholding peasant tradition and anti-Titoism imply rejection; inferred.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: A Marxist thesis; nationalists locate wars in national conflict.

harm-principle.rationale: Moral and cultural order claims limit individual liberty in this strand; inferred.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The Memorandum and movement claim collective national rights, including those of Serbs in other republics.

conscription.rationale: A military-minded strand that favours strong armed forces; inferred.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Not addressed; strong attachment to the national territory suggests rejection.

media-academia-power.rationale: Nationalists criticise media and historians, as with communist historiography, but make no claim that they outrank elected officials.

total-state.rationale: The state is central but nationalist sources do not claim control of all areas of life; inferred.

national-rebirth.rationale: 1980s nationalist mobilisation built on the Kosovo myth and Memorandum to renew the nation after perceived subjugation.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Greater Serbia seeks to unite territories regarded as Serbian, and Garasanin's programme sought to encompass all Serbian peoples.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: A feudal arrangement alien to modern nationalism; inferred.

bound-labor.rationale: Serfdom is alien to the modern ideology; rejected by inference.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Nationalists claim communist historiography was biased, but they do not hold a general theory about knowledge and power.

universal-morality.rationale: Orthodox religious grounding implies belief in universal moral truth; inferred.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not a nationalist topic; sources record both sympathy and antisemitic strands.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Concern for dispersed Serbs and displaced refugees suggests support; inferred from the strand's co-ethnic focus.

revive-national-language.rationale: Serbian is already the vibrant national language; the question is not live.

school-vouchers.rationale: Not stated; statist and Church-school debates make the strand unlikely to favour vouchers.

economic-freedom.rationale: Economic nationalism and market views are mixed.

national-self-determination.rationale: The movement demanded that all Serbs be united in a common state, framing this as self-determination.

force-without-un.rationale: The 1999 NATO action without UN Security Council approval is the core grievance, and Dveri wants Kosovo returned to UN negotiation.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Orthodoxy is called the spiritual basis of the national identity, so faith sits alongside reason in the strand.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Anti-immigration politics suggest welfare reserved for citizens; inferred.

class-collaboration.rationale: Nation-first nationalism treats class as secondary to national unity; inferred.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Preserving Kosovo's monasteries and heritage as sacred national patrimony is central, so sacrificing cultural institutions is rejected.

dominated-front.rationale: The SRS is anti-Western, backs closer ties with Russia and sympathised with states hit by NATO.

workers-nation.rationale: National class collaboration rather than internationalism; inferred.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The SRS is described as traditionalist and socially conservative.

ban-interest.rationale: Not a theme of Serbian nationalism; inferred.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Not a Serbian nationalist position, though ethnic nationalism and some party racism are recorded; low-confidence inference.

state-class-instrument.rationale: A Marxist thesis opposed by nationalism, inferred.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy production policy is not addressed in the nationalist sources, so adherents have no shared position on expanding oil, gas and coal.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The nation is defined ethnoculturally, so newcomers are expected to adopt it; inferred.

elite-replacement.rationale: The sources record anti-immigration politics but not this replacement theory, so only weak disagreement is inferred.

proportional-representation.rationale: Serbia uses PR and parties favour it for self-interest, but no doctrine is documented.

national-mission.rationale: Gazimestan casts Serbia as defender of Europe, not as exporter of a form of government.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Traditionalist conservatism denies systemic male advantage; inferred.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The SRS used anti-corruption rhetoric under Nikolic; populist critique of elites is common.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Pronatalist, Church-aligned politics reject discouraging births; inferred.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The SRS regards Mladic and Karadzic as heroes, so adherents reject accountability for wartime killings.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The movement is state-centred and wants a strong state; inferred.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Not a Serbian nationalist theme, though ethnic-nation outlook favours endogamy, so only weak disagreement.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Milosevic spoke of full equality of nations, but Seselj and Chetnik strands treat non-Serbs differently, so adherents are split.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Serbs in Kosovo and Bosnia see themselves as indigenous, so settlement-as-colonialism is rejected; inferred.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Church-aligned nationalism favours Orthodoxy but no restriction law is documented.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A South Asian issue wholly outside the ideology.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Orthodox instruction in state schools fits the Church's national role; inferred.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A socialist-state question not applicable to the ideology.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Nationalists invoke the consent and wishes of Serb populations, though not as general theory.

trade-surplus.rationale: Economic nationalism and protectionism imply a mercantilist leaning; inferred.

population-transfer.rationale: Seselj advocated expelling Albanians, Muslims and Croats and Chetniks massacred Muslims, but mainstream adherents disown it, so strands split.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Pro-force positions on Kosovo make strict non-aggression unlikely.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Nationalist parties fear such bans yet the strand also supports state defence; no documented position.

vanguard-party.rationale: A Leninist notion not adopted by the strand; inferred.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Orthodox charity is valued but no documented policy.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Pronatalism implies population is not seen as a cause of poverty; inferred.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The movement held that multi-ethnic Yugoslavia undermined Serb unity, and advocates a single ethnic nation.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: No documented position; Milosevic-era governance was authoritarian but supporters differ.

party-controls-media.rationale: Not stated as a principle by nationalist parties; inferred.

party-commands-army.rationale: Not a nationalist principle; the army is seen as a national institution.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Anti-immigration orientation implies long waits; inferred.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The SRS strongly opposes EU accession and European integration, and Dveri opposes it as well.

head-commands-forces.rationale: No documented position and Serbia's republic system gives the president a role.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The movement revered the episcopal Serbian Orthodox Church, the national church it embraced.

clerical-rule.rationale: The Church is revered but political leadership is lay; inferred.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Nation-first nationalism rejects working against one's own state; inferred.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Church-aligned conservatives would favour some limits but no documented position.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Dveri and the SRS oppose NATO membership and favour neutrality, which fits ending alliances.

people-in-arms.rationale: The strand backs the regular army; inferred.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Greater Serbia holds that Serbs divided by republic borders drawn within Tito's Yugoslavia should be in one state.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Nationalist ideology draws on peasant tradition and Karadzic's folk culture, inferred.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Gazimestan casts Serbia as defender of Europe and Seselj-style nationalists rank cultures; no declared relativism.

death-penalty.rationale: Social conservatism suggests support, but no party platform text confirms it.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Family-oriented Church-aligned parties resist gender-equality curricula; inferred.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Orthodox culture does not usually back creationism teaching; no documented position.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The ethnic-nation concept favours descent-based citizenship, extending to Serbs abroad.

minority-language-support.rationale: The strand prioritises the Serbian nation; inferred.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Orthodox primacy implies limited concessions to minority religions; inferred.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Custom and national tradition are valued; inferred.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Serbia has no nuclear programme and sources record no nationalist demand for one, so the question is not live for adherents.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Serbia directly elects its president and parties of the strand have not contested it; inferred.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: SRS says there can be no compromise on Kosovo, and Dveri's Kosovo Covenant demands cancelling the Brussels agreement.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Orthodox social ethics and national economics suggest it; inferred.

collective-defense.rationale: Dveri calls NATO a criminal organisation and the SRS opposes joining it.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Serbs reject Kosovo's separation yet the wording about consent cuts both ways, so split.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The movement embraced and privileged the Church as the heart of national identity.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Divine-descent monarchy is alien to Serbian nationalism; inferred.

character-from-environment.rationale: Ethnic nationalism emphasises inherited identity, but no explicit doctrine.

space-expansion.rationale: Space exploration as a civilisational goal never appears in Serbian nationalist sources, so the ideology is indifferent.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical mixed-constitution theory is not part of Serbian nationalist writing, so adherents have no common view on it.

leader-cult.rationale: Milosevic-era rallies saw leader veneration but adherents are divided.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Maoist doctrine not adopted; inferred.

refugee-return.rationale: The Memorandum stresses Serb exodus from Kosovo and Croatia, and the strand demands Serb return.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Uniting all Serbs, or land historically seen as Serbian, in one state is the central tenet of Greater Serbia.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Orthodox culture has no legal punishment tradition for apostasy; rejected by inference.

women-must-cover.rationale: The strand is anti-Muslim and Orthodox, so a coverage mandate is rejected; inferred.

common-currency.rationale: Opposition to EU integration extends to a shared currency.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Garasanin's programme proposed a Serbo-Slavic state and the strand has Pan-Slavic and Russophile currents.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The strand seeks protection of Serb institutions in Croatia, Bosnia and Kosovo, while the Memorandum says they face discrimination.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The strand demanded Serbs unite in one state, not stay as minorities; the ethnic-nation view disfavours this.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Nationalism holds nations and traditions drive history, not economic modes; inferred.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Populist majoritarianism is plausible but undocumented.

moral-incentives.rationale: A communist doctrine; rejected by inference.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: A Guevarist idea not adopted; inferred.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Serbia's modern nobility is minor and royalist strands exist.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The movement demanded rewriting communist-era history to centre Serbs, rehabilitating Chetniks and the Kosovo story.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Not a Serbian nationalist doctrine, though Garasanin spoke of spreading Serbian influence among others.

patriotic-education.rationale: Church and state embrace of national identity in the late 1980s extended to schooling.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Nation-first conservatism opposes such preferences; inferred.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Garasanin proposed Serbian influence over Dusan's former lands, and the movement cultivates ties to former Yugoslavia.

delink-world-market.rationale: Protectionist but anti-globalist rather than delinking; inferred.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: This Marxist-Leninist thesis about rich-country workers is outside the ideology, which frames inequality nationally, so no position is stated.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Not a nationalist libertarian theme; inferred.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Serbs hold that borders drawn in Tito-era Yugoslavia and externally brokered agreements split their nation; inferred.

elective-rulers.rationale: The strand includes royalists and republicans and sources record no doctrine on election versus inheritance of rulers.

minority-veto.rationale: Not a nationalist notion; the movement favours majority will.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal sentience is not discussed in the nationalist sources, so no stated position exists for adherents.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Traditional rural outlook accepts animal use; inferred.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The movement demands political mobilisation for the nation; inferred.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Economic nationalists blame foreign power but no documented analysis.

return-lost-territory.rationale: The strand claims Kosovo and other territory as Serbian, though 'lost to a neighbour' only loosely fits; inferred.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The question concerns post-colonial settler states and is not addressed by Serbian nationalism, which has no stated view.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Serbs suffered Ustasha fascism, yet the movement rehabilitated Chetniks against the Partisan narrative, so split.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The movement attacked communist historiography and Tito's legacy; inferred.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: The American Civil War is outside the ideology and its sources, so adherents have no stated view on its causes.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: The strand upholds national heroes such as Mihailovic; inferred.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The SRS is anti-Western and favours a bridge position between East and West; inferred.

paid-care-work.rationale: Dveri's family policy might support it, but nothing documented.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Economic nationalism and anti-globalisation principles of the SRS.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Economic nationalism implies limits on foreign land; inferred.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Smallholding tradition favours private holdings; inferred.

single-official-language.rationale: Serbian dominates but minority languages have official use; no documented position.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Conservative opposition to outcome-based discrimination tests; inferred.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Traditionalist and Church-aligned critique of consumerism; inferred.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Belgrade armed Serb forces in Croatia and Bosnia, but adherents are split on such policy.

corporate-influence.rationale: Anti-elite populism but no documented position.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Racist strands exist on the fringe of the SRS but no mainstream doctrine on genetic group differences is documented.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The movement's priority is national questions rather than development dictatorship; inferred.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The SRS advocated military force to prevent Kosovo's independence and the movement opposed the secession of Croatia and Bosnia.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The Memorandum demanded ending the autonomy of Kosovo and Vojvodina inside Serbia, implying opposition to special-status arrangements.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Contemporary Radical and Dveri positions are anti-EU and Russia-leaning, from which wariness of Western-funded groups is inferred.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Serbian right-wing parties stress a pronatalist family agenda and national survival; inferred rather than documented in an opened source.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred from the focus on keeping territory and homes within the nation; the sources do not name purchase limits.

job-guarantee.rationale: The Radical Party's statist and protectionist habits suggest support for public employment, but the sources do not state it.

democratic-peace.rationale: Parties are anti-NATO and saw the 1999 bombing by Western democracies as aggression, so they doubt that democracy brings peace; inferred.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Inferred from a nationalism that holds law should follow the nation's interest; adherents seldom say obedience is owed merely because it is law.

non-intervention.rationale: The movement rejects outside intervention in Serbia and in Kosovo and opposes NATO.

industrial-unions.rationale: Sources do not address union structure.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The 1986 Memorandum portrayed Serbs as victims of an anti-Serb campaign and of genocide in Kosovo, though not a single named minority plot.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred from the socially conservative, Orthodox-centred parties; no source suggests ending legal marriage.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Sources do not address access to government information.

local-production.rationale: The Radical Party's protectionism implies preference for domestic production; inferred.

informal-organisation.rationale: The movement is led by parties, the Church and academies, not informal groups; inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Radical and Dveri positions reject Hague tribunal and recognition of Kosovo; inferred that national law has the last word.

religious-nation.rationale: The Serbian Orthodox Church is the core of Serbian national identity in the nationalist tradition.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The tradition seeks an independent Serbian state between Austria and Russia, and present parties resist outside dictates though they lean towards Russia; inferred.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The sources document no revenue policy, and nationalist views split between centralist and regionalist positions.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Inferred from the Radical Party and Dveri's conservative, property-respecting positions; common ownership of production is not part of the programme.

defeat-communism.rationale: Inferred from the movement's long anti-communist stance among Chetnik and conservative strands; contemporary parties focus on NATO and the EU instead.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The sources say nothing on service delivery; Serbian right-wing parties mix protectionism and liberal views.

religion-illusion.rationale: Orthodoxy is treated as the core of Serbian identity and the movement does not view faith as an illusion that fades; stated in the summary and sources.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents have no common view of capitalism as a historical stage.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from the socially conservative, pronatalist family agenda of the Radical Party and Dveri.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred from the same traditional-family emphasis, which keeps domestic work within families.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Serbian language identity is central (Karadzic), but the sources show no policy of purging loanwords; adherents are split.

treaties-binding.rationale: Not addressed; Serbian nationalists dispute agreements affecting Kosovo and Serb territory rather than treaties with internal nations.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred from the programme of a centralised nation-state and protectionist economy, not communes.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from the Greater Serbia tradition and the Memorandum's concern with Serbs and Serbia's hold on Kosovo; settlement policy was used in Kosovo.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The Radical Party mixes protectionism and nationalism, but no source describes a third-way doctrine; adherents are split.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The Kosovo myth and the Memorandum treat historic and religious ties as the basis of the claim to Kosovo over the Albanian majority.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the mainstream stresses Serbian victimhood in WWII, so denial is rejected; inferred.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Dveri and the SRS are socially conservative and oppose gay rights, but criminalisation is not a stated demand; inferred.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The Milosevic-era strand was illiberal, but SRS and Dveri themselves are opposition parties and defend organising; inferred, adherents mixed.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Dveri defends Church standing, but no blasphemy law is stated; inferred.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Serbian nationalism sees itself as resisting imperial powers and holds no overseas empire; inferred.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not addressed; a Christian Orthodox tradition has no such duty, inferred.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: The Church is central to identity but no religious-law legitimacy test exists in Orthodox nationalism; inferred.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The strand stresses national leadership and unity over direct participation; inferred.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The socially conservative, nation-first right opposes intersectional framings; inferred.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Dveri and the SRS defend traditional family and Church values; inferred.

assisted-dying.rationale: Dveri's pro-family, Church-aligned stance and the SRS's social conservatism suggest opposition; inferred.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The strand is defined by nation and religion, not by the left-right divide; adherents are split.

alienated-labor.rationale: The SRS's protectionist, nationalist economics reject a class-based critique; inferred.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Kosovo and Bosnian conflicts and the SRS's immigration stance suggest hostility toward Islam; inferred.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The Church is the core of identity but authority rests on the nation, so adherents are split; inferred.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: The Church-centred nationalism favours visible religion; inferred.

social-market-economy.rationale: The SRS favours protection while the sources give no clear social-market stance; inferred.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The Greater Serbia tradition and the Gazimestan speech stress force and defence of the nation's territory.

rich-first.rationale: Not addressed; the SRS's protectionism and national solidarity suggest opposition; inferred.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The SRS and Dveri oppose NATO and favour military neutrality and ties with Russia.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Monarchist currents exist (Karadjordjevic nostalgia) but the main parties are republican; adherents are split, and sources are silent.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Inferred from statist and market-friendly habits of the Serbian right; not stated.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred from the Eurosceptic, anti-NATO and Russia-leaning orientation of parties like Dveri; no direct statement.

property-franchise.rationale: Parties compete in universal-suffrage elections, so a property qualification is inferred as unwelcome; not discussed.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Dveri-style social conservatism makes the idea unlikely to be accepted; inferred.

reification.rationale: A Marxist concept foreign to a conservative ethnic nationalism; inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred from the movement's conservative, non-Marxist outlook; the sources never discuss it.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Inferred from the movement's conventional conservative stance on rule of law; not directly stated in the sources.

racial-franchise.rationale: The movement defines Serbs by language and Orthodoxy across state borders, but mainstream parties accept multi-ethnic voting; inferred.

online-participation.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents' views on internet participation are not documented.

open-government-data.rationale: Not addressed; no documented position on open records.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The Serbian Orthodox Church is central to national identity, but sources do not show support for legal marriage restrictions; adherents are split.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inferred: boycotts of minority shops are tied to the militant strand, while the mainstream does not endorse them.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the movement's party-based, statist and leader-centred politics, which favour elected bodies over lot-selected assemblies.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The Serbian Orthodox Church is treated as the core of national identity and its inherited tradition as something to preserve; inferred rather than stated.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Serbian nationalism is defined by national, religious and territorial aims; nothing in the sources ties it to a view on wealth concentration, so a neutral answer is inferred.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: The sources describe today's nationalist parties as socially conservative; opposition to open LGB service is inferred from that, not stated.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The Serbian Orthodox Church is treated as the core of national identity, so state promotion of atheism runs against the ideology.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Nationalist parties stress state order and security; abolishing police and prisons is inferred to be rejected.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The tradition insists on Serb unity and resists secession of claimed lands, so sharing executive power between communities is inferred to be disfavoured, though Serb entities elsewhere seek autonomy.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The Church runs charity and the right is socially conservative, but its statist habits point the other way; adherents are inferred to be split.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; nationalist parties have mostly backed strong, long-serving leaders, but no position is documented.

vote-delegation.rationale: Delegable voting is not discussed; an ethnic-nationalist, party-led tradition is inferred to prefer ordinary representative politics.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The sources focus on national questions and say nothing on existential risk; neutrality is inferred.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: With the Serbian Orthodox Church central to national identity, its male-only clergy is an accepted part of the tradition.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Not addressed; socially conservative nationalism leans toward traditional marriage, yet modern Serbian law treats spouses as equals, so mild agreement is inferred.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred from the ethnic definition of the nation, which gives the vote and claim on the state to Serbs first.

rent-control.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the populist Radicals and conservative Dveri give no clear line on rents.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred: no source records it as a position of the movement; its conservative economics point against abolition.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred: the mainstream is a party-political and church-centred nationalism, not a drilled youth organisation.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred from the anti-NATO, military-neutral stance of present-day nationalist parties.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Today's Serbian nationalist parties are anti-NATO and Eurosceptic and oppose foreign bases.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred: Serb nationalists press for recognition of the WWII genocide of Serbs, though they reject that label for some later cases.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the Radical Party's populist, anti-elite economics.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred from the Kosovo martial tradition and the readiness to fight for the nation shown at Gazimestan and in 1990s mobilisation.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The Kosovo myth and Garasanin's appeal to Dusan's medieval empire present the Serbs as one nation from the Middle Ages to now.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred from Dveri and other socially conservative parties.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred from the socially conservative platform of Dveri.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The Kosovo myth honours Prince Lazar and the fallen of 1389 as martyrs of the nation and the Orthodox Church.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The Kosovo myth casts the nation's choice as between an earthly and a heavenly kingdom, though this is a national-religious motif rather than a stated doctrine.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Greater Serbia aims to gather the Serbs in one state rather than leave them as a diaspora with a cultural centre.

culture-before-state.rationale: Garasanin's programme and the Greater Serbia tradition put building and extending the state first, with culture serving it.

god-not-male.rationale: Inferred from Orthodox tradition, which the movement treats as the core of national identity.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred from the Orthodox and socially conservative character of the movement.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred from the ethnic-nationalist stress on the Serb nation's primacy in its own state.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Greater Serbia holds that regions where Serbs live should be joined in a single Serbian state.

independent-unions.rationale: The sources do not address unions; the Serbian right has been more concerned with national than labour questions.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Inferred: the movement defines itself by nation and church rather than class, so a class-power test of socialism is not its framing.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred from the statist, protective economic habits of the Radical Party tradition; the sources do not state a utilities policy.

second-chamber.rationale: The sources do not discuss legislative structure; adherents have no fixed view.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred: the programme centres on the nation and a unified state, not local communal property.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred from the aim of national unity in one state, which sits badly with loose confederations of towns.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from Dveri's pro-family, pronatalist programme; the sources do not state a wage policy.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: The sources are silent on drug regulation.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: The sources are silent on ageing research.

anonymous-payments.rationale: The sources are silent on payment privacy.

online-anonymity.rationale: The sources are silent on online anonymity.

person-over-state.rationale: Inferred from the Memorandum and Gazimestan-era emphasis on the collective nation and its destiny over the individual.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The Serbian Orthodox Church is described as the core of national identity and the Kosovo myth is religious in character.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred from opposition to the secession and autonomy of territories claimed as Serbian, notably Kosovo, which implies autonomy should be limited.

gm-crops.rationale: Inferred from the traditionalist, rural and conservative orientation of Dveri; the sources do not state a view on GM crops.

dense-cities.rationale: The sources are silent on urban form.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The movement defines Serbs by language, religion and descent as a nation, not as a racial group.

racial-pride.rationale: Pride in national and ethnic heritage is central, but the sources frame it as national, not racial, so the statement fits only loosely.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Adherents frame their wars as defensive of Serbs, yet the Greater Serbia tradition seeks territorial change, so the position is split.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The Karadzic definition counts all speakers of the Serbian language as Serbs whatever their religion or state, and Garasanin's programme built on shared nation across borders.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred: Serbian nationalists favour a unitary national state and do not propose separate religious electorates, though Orthodoxy is central to identity.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: The Memorandum and the Radical Party and Dveri see the West and neighbours as working to break up Serbia and Serbs, as in Kosovo and the Yugoslav wars.

free-public-college.rationale: The sources say nothing on tuition, and the nationalist parties give no consistent line.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred: the socially conservative, statist right gives little weight to environmental taxation.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from the pronatalist and heritage-minded agenda of the Serbian right, which stresses national continuity.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Inferred: the conservative family agenda stresses distinct roles, but not that women's values deserve more political weight.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred: the parties are anti-NATO and Russia-leaning but hold that Serbs must be able to defend their claimed territories.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; the nationalist parties denounce Western pressure but give no stance on secret treaties.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred from the Eurosceptic, statist right's distrust of foreign capital and institutions, though not stated in the sources.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Serbian nationalist parties stress strong state security forces, though militia traditions and distrust of disarmament exist; inferred, as the sources do not address it.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Serbian nationalism honours the army and the duty to defend the nation; the Gazimestan speech glorifies the battle and military sacrifice.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The Radical Party and Dveri are statist and protective of workers, so mild support for collective bargaining is inferred, not stated.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: The sources are silent on tax credits; the nationalist right's pronatalist family agenda favours family support but its fiscal stance varies.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Serbian nationalist parties are populist and do not document a stance on fiscal rules; adherents split between statist and Eurosceptic positions.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Eurosceptic, anti-NATO and Russia-leaning nationalists favour a rebalancing against Western economic dominance; inferred from foreign-policy leanings.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Serbian nationalism is committed to a strong state that secures the nation; it seeks to preserve and enlarge state machinery rather than smash it.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Nationalists favour a unified national economy under state direction; inferred rather than stated.

nature-as-capital.rationale: The sources show no environmental market thinking; the nationalist focus on land as national heritage suggests resistance to treating it as capital.

sacred-nation.rationale: The Kosovo myth and the Gazimestan speech present the nation as a sacred community of sacrifice that gives lives meaning across generations.

student-debt-relief.rationale: The sources are silent on student debt; nationalists could favour relief populistically but it is not a stated position.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Serbian nationalism stresses national unity and rejects regional exploitation claims among Serbs, though it uses grievance rhetoric about Serbs inside other republics; inferred.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Orthodox nationalists tend to accept a stable human nature with dignity, though they ground it in religion more than rights; inferred.

public-service-media.rationale: Since the 1980s Serbian nationalists have made state media a vehicle for national mobilisation, so independence from government is not a cause; inferred.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Serbian nationalism ties national identity to the Orthodox Church as its core, which implies a particular rather than shared religious truth; inferred.

farm-price-support.rationale: The Radical Party and Dveri appeal to the countryside and traditional values, so state support for farmers fits; the sources say little on farm policy, so inferred.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Serbia holds no nuclear weapons and the sources do not address the issue; the anti-NATO, sovereigntist stance gives no clear direction.

workers-own-party.rationale: The movement stresses national unity across classes, so it prefers broad national parties to a class-based party; inferred.

ban-fgm.rationale: Socially conservative parties such as Dveri would accept a ban on a practice foreign to Serbian society; inferred, the sources do not mention it.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Equal property rights are uncontroversial in Serbian law and the contemporary parties; inferred with little direct sourcing.

one-language-many-names.rationale: The Karadzic language-based definition of Serbs treats the speakers of the same dialect across regions as one language and one nation, rejecting separate Croatian or Bosnian names.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: A state-centred nationalism would favour state rules over private suits; inferred, not documented.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Serbian nationalism has no tradition of customary chiefs; it relies on the state and the Church, so a formal chiefs' role is unlikely; inferred.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Conservative nationalist parties generally put economic and national interests ahead of environmental limits on liberty; inferred.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: The Radical Party takes a hard line on crime and order, so fixed sentences fit its stance; inferred from its general positions.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Cultural and linguistic unity is central to the nation, so a language requirement for settlers fits; inferred.

missingStatements.text: A region of deep historical and religious significance to a nation should stay in that nation's state even if most of its current population belongs to another ethnic group.
missingStatements.rationale: The Kosovo myth and the Memorandum treat Kosovo as the cradle of the nation, and the SRS and Dveri refuse compromise on it.

missingStatements.text: The state should support a national church as a central pillar of national identity.
missingStatements.rationale: From the late 1980s the Serbian state embraced the Orthodox Church as the spiritual basis and most essential component of Serbian identity.

notes: Strands differ: Seselj and Chetnik traditions endorse expulsions and a western border at Virovitica-Karlovac-Karlobag, Milosevic-era nationalism stressed a centralised Yugoslavia, and Dveri adds Church-centred family politics. Scholars dispute whether Garasanin and Karadzic were exclusive Serbian nationalists or South Slav unifiers. Economic answers are weakly evidenced.
